To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the excimer and exciplex of aromatic compounds do not possess sufficient gain to be used in laser systems.
laser emission from excimer and exciplex states of aromatic compounds is not likely.
the cross section for stimulated absorption is (3–10)×10−18 cm2, and the cross section for spontaneous emission is (1.3–3)×10−16 cm2.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel method for the determination of the rate constants of the reactions between excited atoms and molecules in the gas phase.
the possibility of laser action from intermolecular and intra molecular excimers and exci-plexes of aromatic compounds, which are characterized by a large value of the dipole moment.
the development of a new class of lasers, namely excimer and exciplex lasers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the possibility of laser action in excimers and excilpexes of aromatic molecules is very small.
lasing of excimers and/or exciplexes has been observed in only one instance, that of the excimer of benzene, and that this lasing was weak.
lasing is not to be expected from excimers and/or exciplexes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the probability of lasing from excimers and excitons in aromatic compounds is very small.
the most promising candidates for lasing in the near future are the exciplexes formed by aromatic molecules in a solid state.
the probability of laser emission from the excimer or exciplex of aromatic molecules in the gas phase is low.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cross section of stimulated emission from excited states is a very important parameter in laser physics and that it can serve as an additional selection criterion for laser systems.
the possibility of laser action from intermolecular excimers and intramolecular exciton complexes is very unlikely.
exciplexes and excimers of aromatic compounds have the potential to serve as active media for lasers, but only in the case of a very high concentration.
